problem: The text is broken and unreadable. The question reads 'A real gas has T(∂V/∂T)P JT, and does expansion warm or cool the gas?' with the comparison symbol and the value of μJT missing, so the student cannot tell what is given. The answer is also broken: 'so μJT JT dP > 0' has lost the inequality and the dT step.
fix: Q6: A real gas has T(∂V/∂T)P < V. Find μJT and state whether expansion through a throttle warms or cools the gas. Answer: μJT = [T(∂V/∂T)P − V]/Cp; the numerator is negative, so μJT < 0. For expansion dP < 0, and dT = μJT dP > 0, so the gas warms.

where: Section 1, closing sentences after the four relations
problem: The claim 'The left side contains entropy in the denominator or numerator. The right side contains only P, V, T and their slopes' is wrong for two of the four relations: in the dU relation (∂T/∂V)S = −(∂P/∂S)V and the dH relation (∂T/∂P)S = (∂V/∂S)P, entropy sits in the denominator on the right side, and on the left side entropy only appears as the held-constant subscript.
fix: Say instead: in the dA and dG relations entropy appears in the numerator of the left side, so those two convert an entropy slope into a P–V–T slope. In the dU and dH relations entropy stays in the derivative, so they are less useful for that job.

problem: 'Dropping the subscript changes the number and the units' is misleading. Changing the held-constant variable changes the value, but the units usually stay the same: (∂V/∂T)P and (∂V/∂T)S are both in m³/K.
fix: Write: 'Dropping the subscript changes the value of the derivative, so always state the variable held constant.'

problem: The example '(∂V/∂T)V' is a poor illustration: at constant V there is no volume change, so that derivative is simply zero, which does not show the point being made.
fix: Use a real confusion instead, e.g. '(∂V/∂T)P is not the same as (∂V/∂T)S or (∂V/∂P)T'.
